summary: Kenji Takahashi is an Indologist who studied at Leiden University and under supervisors Diwakar Acharya, Yuko Yokochi, and Peter Bisschop, among other teachers. He held a JSPS-sponsored fellowship at the University of Naples Federico II from 2019 to 2021.
Kenji Watanabe is an Indologist who studied under Jozef Deleu. He held an assistant post at Taisho University, attested in 1978.

Kenjiu Kasawara (1851–1883) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Oxford in 1879 and was taught by Friedrich Max Müller and Arthur Anthony Macdonell between 1879 and 1882.
Kennard Lipman worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, completing doctoral studies under Herbert V. Guenther. He served as a sessional instructor at the University of Calgary.
Kenneth Doo Young Lee specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Ryuichi Abe and held an attested post at Stetson University in 2007.

Kenneth G. Zysk is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. Educated at UC Santa Barbara and the Australian National University, he held posts at UCLA, Eastern Michigan University, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, University of Toronto, and University of Copenhagen.

Kenneth J. Guest works in religious studies and sinology. He studied at Columbia University, Peking University, Union Theological Seminary, and CUNY, and was taught by Aloysius Pieris. He held appointments at Hunter College and Baruch College.

Kenneth J. Saunders (1883–1937) was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied under Wagiswara. He served as Professor of the History of Religion at the Pacific School of Religion (~1921–1935) and lectured at the University of California (~1921–1934).

Kenneth K. Inada (1923–2011) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who taught Jay L. Garfield. He served as Professor of Philosophy at the University at Buffalo and chaired the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research from 1996 to 1999.

Kenneth K. Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and UC Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini. He held posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies, Musashino University (~1998–2018), and Bukkyō Dendō Kyōkai.

Kenneth Roy Norman (1925–2020) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies who studied at Downing College. He held positions at the University of Cambridge, served as President of the Pali Text Society (1988), and visited SOAS in 1994.

Kenryo Minowa is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1979–1989). He held positions at Rissho University, Eastern Institute, Toyo University, Aichi Gakuin University (~1996–2010), and became a professor at the University of Tokyo in 2010.
Kenryu Nishio specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his doctorate in literature from Otani University and became an emeritus professor at Hanazono University, attested in 2014.
Kenryu Tsuji (1919–2004) was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed studies at Ryukoku University in 1938 and at the University of Toronto.

Kenryu Tsukinowa (1888–1969) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Bukkyo University. He founded the Tantric Buddhism Research Society in 1960 and held posts at Ryukoku University (~1928–1958), Bukkyo University, Koyasan University, and Shuchiin University.
Kenshi Kusano specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Otani University from ~1971 to 1980 and became a professor there around 1999.
Kensuke Nedachi is a scholar of history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University from ~1975 to 1984 and served as a professor there from ~2008 to 2021.
Kenta Suzuki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and the University of Tokyo. Around 2012, he held an associate professorship at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College.

Kenyu Mitomo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Rissho University and UC Berkeley. He served at Rissho University as Dean of Buddhist Studies (~1976–1990) and professor (~1990–2015), and held posts at Otani University and Chung-Hwa Institute.

Kevin A. Vose specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned degrees at Bates College and the University of Virginia, studying under traditional teacher Ngawang Jinpa and doctoral supervisor Jeffrey Hopkins.
